description: Amazon S3 in US-EAST-1 became unavailable, taking down many sites and AWS services that depend on it.
root_cause: An engineer ran an established playbook command to remove a small number of billing servers, but a mistyped input removed far more capacity, including servers backing the S3 index and placement subsystems. Both subsystems then needed a full restart that had not been exercised at that scale for years.
resolution: Restarted the index and placement subsystems, validated metadata integrity, then restored GET, LIST, PUT and DELETE traffic.
lessons: Capacity-removal tools must remove capacity slowly and refuse to go below a subsystem's minimum. Partition large subsystems into smaller cells so restarts are faster. Keep the status page independent of the service it reports on.

description: While fighting database replication lag, an engineer deleted the data directory on the primary PostgreSQL server instead of the secondary.
root_cause: A manual rm -rf intended for the lagging secondary was run on the primary. Several backup methods had silently been failing, so no recent backup existed.
resolution: Restored from a staging snapshot taken about six hours earlier and rebuilt replication; around six hours of issues, merge requests and comments were lost.
lessons: Test restores regularly, not just backups. Alert when backup jobs fail. Make destructive commands show which host they are on. Avoid ad-hoc manual work on production databases late at night.

description: A 43-second network partition between the US East Coast hub and primary data center caused database failover to the West Coast.
root_cause: Orchestrator promoted West Coast MySQL replicas to primaries during a brief network partition. The East Coast had accepted writes the West Coast did not have, and application latency across the country made the new topology unworkable.
resolution: Paused webhook delivery and Pages builds, restored East Coast primaries from backups, replayed replicas and processed the backlog; degraded service for about 24 hours.
lessons: Failover automation must respect cross-region latency and prevent promotions that split writes. Keep the status page updated with a clear estimate. Practise full data-center failover.

symptoms: CPU exhausted on every edge machine
description: A new Web Application Firewall rule drove CPU to 100% on machines handling HTTP traffic worldwide.
root_cause: A regular expression in a newly deployed WAF managed rule caused catastrophic backtracking. It was pushed globally at once, without a staged rollout.
resolution: Issued a global kill for WAF managed rules, which restored traffic, then fixed the rule and re-enabled it.
lessons: Roll out rule changes progressively like code. Use a regex engine with guaranteed run-time bounds. Keep emergency kill switches reachable when the edge is overloaded.

description: A router configuration change during unrelated backbone maintenance caused traffic across the backbone to be sent to Atlanta.
root_cause: A configuration change on the Atlanta router removed a line meant to deactivate a term, so it advertised all its best routes to the backbone and attracted far more traffic than it could handle.
resolution: Removed the Atlanta router from the backbone and restored the correct configuration.
lessons: Put a maximum-prefix limit on backbone BGP sessions. Review router configuration changes like code. Maintenance on one site can overload the whole backbone.

description: Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp disappeared from the internet for about six hours.
root_cause: A command run during routine backbone capacity assessment unintentionally took down all backbone connections. An audit tool that should have blocked it had a bug. DNS servers then withdrew their BGP routes because they could not reach the data centers.
resolution: Engineers went to the data centers in person, restored the backbone, and brought traffic back gradually to avoid power and cache surges.
lessons: Keep out-of-band access that does not depend on the production network. Audit tools that guard destructive commands need their own tests. Plan gradual traffic ramp-up after total outages.

symptoms: major news and retail sites down
description: Most of Fastly's edge network returned errors after one customer changed their configuration.
root_cause: A software deployment in May introduced a latent bug. A valid customer configuration change under specific circumstances triggered it and caused errors across 85% of the network.
resolution: Identified and disabled the configuration within 40 minutes, then deployed a permanent fix for the bug.
lessons: Test for configuration combinations, not just defaults. Limit how far one customer's change can spread. Make it quick to identify the trigger.

description: Roblox was down for 73 hours when its Consul cluster became unhealthy.
root_cause: A newly enabled Consul streaming feature, combined with heavy load, caused contention. A pathological case in BoltDB's freelist handling slowed Consul writes. Both were needed to trigger the failure.
resolution: Disabled streaming, replaced the Consul cluster's hardware and rebuilt data, then restored players in stages with caching.
lessons: Roll out infrastructure features gradually. Understand the storage engines under critical services. Remove circular dependencies between monitoring and the system it monitors.

symptoms: Jira and Confluence data inaccessible for about 400 companies
description: A maintenance script deleted the sites of around 400 cloud customers.
root_cause: A script meant to remove a legacy app was given site IDs instead of app IDs, and ran in permanent-delete mode instead of recoverable mode.
resolution: Restored sites from backups in batches over up to 14 days; no data lost beyond five minutes before deletion.
lessons: Destructive scripts should soft-delete by default and validate what type of ID they receive. Practise multi-site restore at scale. Communicate early and directly with affected customers.

symptoms: high packet loss in US east
description: Network congestion hit Google Cloud, G Suite and YouTube in the eastern US.
root_cause: A configuration change meant for a small group of servers in one region was wrongly applied to a larger number across neighbouring regions, causing them to stop using more than half their network capacity.
resolution: Engineers stopped the automation and restored network control-plane capacity; recovery was slowed because the congestion hampered their own tools.
lessons: Scope automated changes and verify their target set. Keep emergency tools off the network they repair. Prioritise low-latency traffic when capacity drops.

symptoms: private data visible in search engine caches
description: An HTML parser bug leaked memory from Cloudflare edge servers into responses (Cloudbleed).
root_cause: A bounds-check bug in the Ragel-based HTML parser was triggered after switching some features to a new parser, letting it read past the end of a buffer.
resolution: Globally disabled the three affected features within 47 minutes, fixed the parser, and worked with search engines to purge cached data.
lessons: Fuzz memory-unsafe parsers. Keep per-feature kill switches. Plan cleanup of leaked data beyond your own systems.

symptoms: boot loops on millions of machines
description: A Falcon sensor content update crashed about 8.5 million Windows machines.
root_cause: Channel File 291 supplied 21 input fields while the sensor's content interpreter expected 20, causing an out-of-bounds memory read in the kernel driver. The content validator had a bug that let it through.
resolution: Reverted the channel file within 78 minutes; affected machines needed manual or scripted remediation in safe mode.
lessons: Stage content updates like code, with canaries. Check array bounds in kernel-level parsers. Let customers control update timing.

description: Congestion between AWS's internal network and main network degraded many services in US-EAST-1.
root_cause: Automated scaling of an internal-network service triggered unexpected client behavior, a surge of connection activity that overwhelmed the devices linking the internal and main networks.
resolution: Moved internal DNS traffic off congested paths and gradually reduced load; about seven hours to recover.
lessons: Clients need backoff that works under congestion. Monitoring must not share the failing network. Status updates cannot depend on affected infrastructure.

symptoms: Gmail and YouTube errors for signed-in users
description: Google services requiring sign-in failed for about 45 minutes.
root_cause: During a migration of the quota system, an old quota system reported zero usage for the User ID Service; its quota was reduced automatically until it could no longer serve requests.
resolution: Disabled quota enforcement for the service and restored it.
lessons: Quota systems need safeguards against sudden drops to zero. Migrations must retire old systems explicitly. Watch for unexplained usage changes.

symptoms: about half of HTTP requests failing
description: A network change in Cloudflare's busiest data centers withdrew critical routes.
root_cause: A change to BGP policy, part of a project to make those data centers more resilient, reordered policy terms so that key prefixes were withdrawn.
resolution: Reverted the change in each affected data center; recovery was slowed because engineers could not reach some locations.
lessons: Roll out network policy changes to smaller locations first. Keep rollback reachable during an outage. Test policy ordering.

symptoms: tens of thousands of hosts lost network
data ingestion delays in all regions
description: Datadog was unavailable across several regions and clouds for about a day.
root_cause: An automatic security update to systemd on Ubuntu restarted systemd-networkd, which removed network routes managed by Cilium on many hosts at the same time.
resolution: Restored network on nodes, rebuilt Kubernetes clusters and backfilled delayed data.
lessons: Disable unattended OS updates on production nodes. Control how many hosts change at once. Keep an independent way in to rebuild clusters.

description: Reddit was down for about five hours after a Kubernetes upgrade (the Pi Day outage).
root_cause: The upgrade from 1.23 to 1.24 removed the "master" node label in favour of "control-plane". Calico route reflectors selected nodes by the old label, so pod routing collapsed.
resolution: Restored the control plane from backup to 1.23 and re-established networking.
lessons: Read deprecation notes for labels your tools depend on. Test upgrades on a cluster shaped like production. Document legacy clusters.

description: All servers in one Joyent data center rebooted at once.
root_cause: An operator used a tool to reboot a small set of servers but typed the command wrongly, rebooting every server in the data center.
resolution: Brought servers and customer instances back; some nodes needed manual help to boot.
lessons: Tools for broad actions should confirm the number of targets. Limit how many servers one command can affect.

description: Cloudflare's core proxy failed widely after a Bot Management feature file doubled in size.
root_cause: A database permissions change in ClickHouse caused the query building the feature file to return duplicate rows. The larger file exceeded a limit in the proxy, which panicked instead of rejecting the file.
resolution: Stopped generating the bad file, pushed a known good version, and restarted the proxy.
lessons: Treat generated configuration like user input and validate it. Fail open, not panic, on oversized files. Add global kill switches for features.

symptoms: many AWS services erroring in us-east-1
description: DynamoDB in US-EAST-1 became unreachable, cascading into EC2 and many other services.
root_cause: A race condition in DynamoDB's automated DNS management left the regional endpoint with an empty DNS record, and automation could not repair it on its own.
resolution: Manually restored the DNS record, then worked through EC2 and network load balancer backlogs over many hours.
lessons: Automation that edits DNS needs guards against applying stale plans. Model recovery backlogs in dependent services. Keep manual overrides.

description: Slack degraded on the first working day of 2021 as traffic returned after the holidays.
root_cause: AWS Transit Gateways could not scale quickly enough for the traffic surge; packet loss then made health checks fail, and autoscaling removed healthy servers.
resolution: AWS manually increased Transit Gateway capacity; Slack stabilised the fleet and restored capacity.
lessons: Pre-warm network capacity before known traffic surges. Make autoscaling resistant to cascading health-check failures.

description: Azure compute failed on leap day 2012.
root_cause: The guest agent created certificates valid until the same date one year later, producing an invalid date of 29 February 2013. Machines failed to initialize and were marked as bad hardware.
resolution: Disabled service management, fixed the certificate code and rolled it out; some clusters needed several hours more.
lessons: Test date arithmetic around leap days and time zones. Don't let a software bug appear as hardware failure. Pause automated recovery that makes things worse.

description: Power failures in a Portland data center took down Cloudflare's control plane and analytics.
root_cause: The data center lost utility power and generators failed. Some services had not been set up for high availability across the other facilities.
resolution: Failed over to disaster recovery and restored services over about two days.
lessons: Test that every product survives the loss of one facility. Don't rely on provider assurances without testing.

description: A trading system sent millions of erroneous orders in 45 minutes, losing about $440 million.
root_cause: A new deployment missed one of eight servers. A repurposed flag then activated old, unused Power Peg code on that server.
resolution: Stopped the system; the deployment was reverted, which briefly made things worse on all servers.
lessons: Automate deployments and verify every server. Remove dead code rather than reusing flags. Have a tested kill switch.

description: Water entered a Paris data center, causing a multi-cluster failure.
root_cause: A water leak in the cooling system caused a fire in the battery room and shut down a zone; some regional services had dependencies in that zone.
resolution: Moved workloads to other zones; the affected zone stayed down for weeks.
lessons: Regional services must not depend on one zone. Physical failures can take down whole zones.
